subject: alienFlora
pitch:
Category: Plant.
Subject: bioluminescent alien plant.
Style: Avatar.
reasoning:
I'm designing a bioluminescent Pandora-style plant avatar — a static stalk-bulb form with curved fronds showing glowing cyan, teal, and magenta veins, plus luminous spore orbs against dark blue-violet foliage.

Planning out the structure: a central sweeping stalk built with a catmull curve, decorated with glowing ring bands and nodule accents spaced along its length, set against a stem-colored palette with teal and cyan glow highlights.

I'm also sketching five curved root buttresses that fan outward from the base and dip below ground level, plus seven arching fronds whose midribs and leaf blades will radiate outward from the stalk at different heights.

Side veins branch as thin glowing cyan spikes from midrib to edge, with thickness kept minimal and no joints needed since these are static models. I'm now sketching out a frond-building function taking azimuth, height, length, lift, droop, width, and color, defining the midrib as a bezier curve from base outward and upward.

Writing frond geometry code...

Writing midrib sweep and vein glow...

For the crown, I'm planning a bell-like flower at the stalk top with curved petals sweeping upward, a glowing orb center, and thin stamen filaments tipped with small magenta spheres — going for a bioluminescent "helicoradian" look.

Now I'm shaping the petals with a flattened ellipse radius function for the sweep geometry, and sketching nine drooping stamen filaments with glowing cyan tips plus a tall glowing central spire, before moving on to hanging tendrils from the frond tips.

For those tendrils, I'll add three thin glowing-beaded strands per frond swaying downward, keeping tip heights above ground so nothing dips below zero. Then I consider adding a few small floating spore orbs near the crown, but lean toward glowing pods instead to keep things minimal.

Decided on 5 bulbous pods clustered on short stems at the stalk's midpoint with dark husk rings, plus tiny glowing spore nubs scattered near the base roots. I'm tuning frond dimensions now—adjusting lift and droop values so lower fronds keep their tips at a safe height while upper fronds stay shorter and more upright, working out the full list of nine fronds.

Still arranging frond parameters...

Refining the crown calyx outline points to form a closed, non-crossing lathe profile, then planning six petals arranged around the crown with curved bezier paths flaring outward from base to tip.

Still shaping stamens and spire...

Still placing pods...

Now I'm working out the hanging strands coming off each frond tip, using curved paths with small glowing beads along them, and setting up vector helpers for the catmull calculations.

For the membrane I'm adding a dark blue base color plus a glowing cyan rim stripe that sweeps along the blade edges to give it some shimmer.

Writing conversion helpers and finalizing the code.
